Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

significant adjective

considerable, notable

also significantly, considerable, substantial, notable, remarkable, a significant amount, dramatic (a dramatic change), dramatically

classical

Caes. BG 3.20: nōn mediocrem sibi dīligentiam adhibendam intellegēbat
Cic. Rep. 2.55: haud mediocris hic … vir fuit (Lewis & Short)

nōn mediocris, nōn mediocre

phrase: litotes with mediocris (also haud mediocris)

significant, considerable, no small

Latin praises by denying the opposite: “not middling” is “considerable, remarkable” (Lewis & Short, s.v. mediocris). Significantly, considerably: nōn mediocriter (Caes. BG 1.39, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • īnsignis, īnsigne — notable, remarkable, striking

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 102: virtūs (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 1.11.14: īnsignis

    What stands out, as if marked.

  • aliquantus, aliquanta, aliquantum — considerable, a fair amount of

    adjective; mostly the neuter with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.33: aliquantum agrī (Lewis & Short); Sall. Jug. 105.4: timor aliquantus (Lewis & Short)

    Between much and little (Lewis & Short): aliquantum agrī, a fair piece of land.

  • significāns, significantis — expressive, clear (of words)

    adjective (participle of significō) · avoid · classical · Quint. 9.2.44: dīlūcida et significāns dēscrīptiō (Lewis & Short)

    A term of rhetoric for a word or a description that conveys its meaning well (Quintilian); it does not mean “considerable”.

Examples

  • nōn mediocrem sibi dīligentiam adhibendam intellegēbat

    he understood that he would have to take no small careCaes. BG 3.20

  • quālis vidētur opera tibi vōcis meae? — īnsignis, inquit, sīc ut, nisi nōssem tuum animum genusque, similī fūgissem metū

    ‘How do you like what my voice did?’ ‘Remarkable,’ he said, ‘so much so that, had I not known your nature and your breed, I would have run away in fear like the rest.’Phaedr. 1.11.13–15

See also important, major, average.
